Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the model forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the data, I need to identify patterns in the forecast errors:

## Example 1 (2024-08-08)
- Model forecasts are generally higher than true outcomes
- The gap seems to widen in some areas
- Looking at the first few points: model starts at 70.70 vs true 71.06 (underestimated by ~0.36)
- But by point 9: model 72.41 vs true 73.07 (underestimated by ~0.66)
- Later points: model 70.41 vs true 63.21 (overestimated by ~7.20!) - this is massive

Wait, let me look more carefully. Looking at the later points in Example 1:
Model: [70.92, 72.14, 71.70, 72.50, 72.12, 72.61, 70.72, 70.06, 69.81, 70.65, 71.17, 69.99, 71.94, 71.50, 71.67, 70.41, 72.37, 72.40]
True: [70.49, 71.49, 70.77, 71.06, 70.30, 70.43, 68.16, 67.00, 66.20, 66.50, 66.52, 64.92, 66.40, 65.45, 64.99, 63.21, 64.34, 63.70]

The model is consistently OVERESTIMATING prices in the middle section (points 1-6), but then dramatically underestimates in the latter half where prices have been declining.
